title: Submit Your Questions: Will Anyone Keep You Safe From AI?
gist: Short teaser announcing a WIRED subscriber-only livestream (December 2) in which the Backchannel team (Sandra Upson, Steven Levy, Lauren Goode) will take reader questions on Big Tech and AI safety; it frames the AI safety debate as having 'lost the plot' and says the industry has not made changes that reassure people. Note: the raw URL points to a headphone-deals story, but the text is the livestream teaser; card reflects the text only.

insights.claim: WIRED's Backchannel team argues the AI safety conversation has lost the plot, while noting experts broadly agree society is in real trouble even if they disagree over which catastrophe is most salient.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Signals persistent public and media anxiety about AI risk that can feed regulatory pressure on AI developers.
insights.quote: The AI safety conversation, as Lauren Goode put it, has lost the plot.

insights.claim: Proposals such as a pause in training AI models and a data center moratorium have been floated, but according to WIRED the AI industry has not made changes that put people at ease around AI safety.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Data center moratorium proposals are a tail risk to watch for AI infrastructure build-outs.
insights.quote: Though a pause in training models, a data center moratorium, and other regulation has been proposed

insights.claim: WIRED frames critical infrastructure as appearing more vulnerable every day alongside concerns about cyberattacks by rogue AI agents.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Supports a narrative tailwind for cybersecurity spending tied to AI-agent threats.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, critical infrastructure seems more and more vulnerable every day.
